content.overview: Cultivation records must be trustworthy enough to reconstruct what happened. This lesson applies established data-integrity concepts to routine cultivation documentation without presenting pharmaceutical guidance as cannabis law.

vocabulary.definition: Recorded at the time the activity or observation occurs, or under a controlled process that preserves the true timing.
Linked clearly to the person or system that created or changed the record.
The degree to which records remain complete, consistent, accurate, attributable and reconstructable across their lifecycle.

sections.title: Record facts when they happen
sections.body: MHRA data-integrity guidance describes data as attributable, legible and permanent, contemporaneous, original and accurate, with completeness, consistency, endurance and availability across the lifecycle. This course transfers those quality principles to cultivation records; it does not claim MHRA rules govern U.S. cannabis operations.

sections.title: Corrections preserve history
sections.body: Paper or digital corrections follow the facility's controlled method so the original entry and change history are not concealed. Missing data remain identified as missing rather than guessed, and measurements include enough context such as unit, sample or plant identity, location and time to remain meaningful.

workedExamples: A measurement is corrected without erasing the original value, following the supplied correction procedure.
A pH or EC value is recorded with the measurement type, unit, sample identity and time rather than as a context-free number.
commonMistakes: Backfilling observations from memory as if they were recorded live.
Overwriting an original value without preserving the correction history.
content.practicalApplication: Correct a set of flawed cultivation records containing missing units, ambiguous identity, late entries, overwritten values and guessed data.
content.summary: Trustworthy records are factual, attributable, timely and reconstructable. Technicians preserve correction history, include necessary context and never invent missing data.
